([[Windsor, Ontario]]) | college = *[[Vincennes Trailblazers men's basketball|Vincennes]] (2013–2015) *[[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2015–2017) | draft_year = 2017 | career_start = 2017 | years1 = [[2017–18 NBA G League season|2017]]–[[2018–19 NBA G League season|2019]] | team1 = [[Windy City Bulls]] | years2 = [[2019–20 NBA G League season|2019–2020]] | team2 = [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] | years3 = {{nbay|2019|end}}–{{nbay|2020|end}} | team3 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years4 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2021|end}} | team4 = [[Orlando Magic]] | years5 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]] | team5 = →[[Lakeland Magic]] | years6 = {{nbay|2021|end}} | team6 = [[Miami Heat]] | years7 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2022]] | team7 = →Sioux Falls Skyforce | years8 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team8 = Sioux Falls Skyforce | years9 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]] | team9 = [[Memphis Hustle]] | years10 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team10 = [[Capital City Go-Go]] | years11 = 2026–present | team11 = [[Vancouver Bandits]] | highlights = }} '''Mychal Mulder''' (born June 14, 1994) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Vancouver Bandits]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]] (CEBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Vincennes Trailblazers men's basketball|Vincennes Trailblazers]] and the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. ==Early life== Mulder is the son of Jennifer Gignac and Randy Mulder. His mother was an Executive Assistant at the local Utilities company and his father worked at [[General Motors]] before being forced to retire after a leg injury.{{cite news |last1=Vaught |first1=Jamie |title=Despite limited playing time, Mulder becoming a productive performer for Cats |url=https://www.nkytribune.com/2017/02/jamie-vaught-despite-limited-playing-time-mulder-becoming-a-productive-performer-for-cats/ |access-date=October 2, 2019 |work=Northern Kentucky Tribune |date=February 14, 2017}} Mulder was named after former NBA player [[Mychal Thompson]], the father of Mulder's future [[Golden State Warriors|Golden State]] teammate [[Klay Thompson]]. Mulder was raised in [[Windsor, Ontario]], alongside an elder sister, Cynthia.{{cite news |last1=Tipton |first1=Jerry |title=Beep! Beep! Mulder's father gives new meaning to dribble drive |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article114509948.html |access-date=January 1, 2020 |work=Lexington Herald-Leader |date=November 13, 2016}} He played basketball at [[Catholic Central High School (Windsor, Ontario)|Catholic Central High School]], where he was coached by Pete Cusumano.{{cite news |title='A mind-blowing experience': Windsor, Ont. basketball player on Miami Heat's 'radar' |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/windsor/mychal-mulder-miami-heat-windsor-1.5286573 |access-date=October 2, 2019 |agency=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation |date=September 17, 2019}} Mulder was considered a Top 10 Canadian prospect in 2013. ==College career== Mulder received a single [[NCAA Division I]] scholarship offer, to play for the [[Detroit Mercy Titans men's basketball]] team.{{cite news |last1=Letourneau |first1=Connor |title=Mychal Mulder took a long route to 10-day contract with Warriors |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/warriors/article/Mychal-Mulder-took-a-long-route-to-10-day-15090572.php |access-date=February 28, 2020 |work=San Francisco Chronicle |date=February 27, 2020}} Mulder opted to begin his college basketball career at [[Vincennes University]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 15.7 points and 6.4 rebounds per game, shooting 46.3 percent from behind the arc. He led the team to a 33–2 record, was named a JUCO All-American and was rated the 13th-best junior-college prospect by 247Sports. [[File:Mychal-Mulder.jpg|thumb|left|Mulder playing for Kentucky]] He then transferred to play for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball]] team.{{cite news |last1=Parker |first1=Jim |title=Windsor's Mulder set to workout for NBA's Clippers and Timberwolves |url=https://montrealgazette.com/sports/basketball/windsors-mulder-set-to-workout-for-nbas-clippers-and-timberwolves/wcm/715b4658-1f09-431b-ba70-b39b223c7ecc |access-date=October 2, 2019 |work=Windsor Star/Montreal Gazette |date=September 17, 2019}} He chose Kentucky over several other colleges, including [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], and [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]].{{cite news|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150520171121/http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2015/04/28/four-star-juco-guard-mulder-picks-kentucky/26526735/|archive-date=May 20, 2015|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2015/04/28/four-star-juco-guard-mulder-picks-kentucky/26526735/|title=Four-star JUCO guard Mulder picks Kentucky|access-date=April 28, 2015|date=April 29, 2015|newspaper=[[Courier-Journal]]|author=Tucker, Kyle}} [https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2015/04/28/mychal-mulder-juco-kentucky-indiana-vincennes/26505009/ Alt URL]{{cite news|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2015/04/28/mychal-mulder-juco-kentucky-indiana-vincennes/26505009/|title=Vincennes guard also considered Wichita State and Creighton|access-date=April 29, 2015|date=April 29, 2015|newspaper=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]|author=Roberts, Ben}} As a senior at Kentucky, Mulder made two starts and averaged 4.7 points and 1.5 rebounds in 10.6 minutes per game, shooting 40.3% from the field and a team-high 92.3% from the free throw line. ==Professional career== ===Windy City Bulls (2017–2019)=== Mulder went undrafted in the [[2017 NBA draft]]. He was later selected ninth overall in the [[2017 NBA G League draft]] by the [[Windy City Bulls]]. In his second season with the Bulls, Mulder posted 13.7 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.6 assists in 32.9 minutes per game. In May 2019, Mulder was invited to the NBA G League Elite Camp.{{cite news |last1=Tipton |first1=Jerry |title=Former Kentucky guard getting chance to boost his NBA stock at G League Elite Camp |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article230258034.html |access-date=October 2, 2019 |work=Lexington Herald-Leader |date=May 11, 2019}} ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2019–2020)=== Mulder signed with the [[Miami Heat]] on September 17, 2019.{{cite news |last1=Chiang |first1=Anthony |title=Competition for Heat two-way deal grows. Miami signs Mychal Mulder to camp roster |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article235157662.html |access-date=October 2, 2019 |work=Miami Herald |date=September 17, 2019}}{{cite news |title=Heat sign former Kentucky guard Mychal Mulder to camp deal |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-mychal-mulder-20190916-6zw4u4guiferxlrmukujijqcnm-story.html |access-date=October 2, 2019 |work=Sun Sentinel |date=September 17, 2019}} The team waived Mulder on October 15, 2019.{{cite news |last1=Chiang |first1=Anthony |title=With both two-way contract spots still open, Heat makes moves with eye toward G League |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article236256168.html |access-date=October 31, 2019 |work=Miami Herald |date=October 15, 2019}}{{cite news |title=Windsor, Ont.'s Mychal Mulder won't play with Miami Heat in regular NBA season |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/windsor/mychal-mulder-waived-from-miami-heat-1.5331517 |access-date=October 31, 2019 |publisher=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation |date=October 23, 2019}} He began the season with the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite news |last1=Chiang |first1=Anthony |title=Heat affiliate picks Trey Mourning, son of Alonzo Mourning, in G League draft |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article236684788.html |access-date=October 31, 2019 |work=Miami Herald |date=October 26, 2019}}{{cite news |title=Skydorce acquire returning player rights to Mychal Mulder |url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-returning-player-rights-to-mychal-mulder/ |access-date=November 8, 2019 |publisher=G League |date=September 16, 2019}} ===Golden State Warriors (2020–2021)=== On February 27, 2020, the [[Golden State Warriors]] announced that they had signed Mulder to a 10-day contract.{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Guard Mychal Mulder to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/mychal-mulder-20200227|date=February 27, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 27, 2020}} He made his debut against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] that same day. Mulder had two points and four rebounds in that game, which was a 116–86 loss.{{cite news |last1=Call III |first1=Tommy |title=Mychal Mulder providing spark off the bench during Warriors 10-day contract |url=https://warriorswire.usatoday.com/2020/02/29/mychal-mulder-providing-spark-off-the-bench-during-warriors-10-day-contract/ |access-date=March 2, 2020 |work=USA Today |date=March 1, 2020}} On March 1, 2020, Mulder had a career-high 17 points, along with two rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal in just his third game with the Warriors, a 124–110 loss against the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|title=Mychal Mulder is proving himself as a competitor to Steve Kerr|url=https://warriorswire.usatoday.com/2020/03/01/mychal-mulder-is-proving-himself-as-a-competitor-to-steve-kerr/|date=March 1, 2020|website=USA Today|access-date=March 2, 2020}} On March 7, he started against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] - setting a new career-high 18 points and 3 assists during his last game of his first 10-day contract, a 118–114 win.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/warriors-mychal-mulder-reveals-hes-named-after-klay-thompsons-dad|title=Warriors' Mychal Mulder reveals he's named after Klay Thompson's dad|date=March 8, 2020 }} On March 10, after his 10-day contract expired, the Warriors signed him to a multi-year contract.{{cite news |title=Warriors sign Canadian Mychal Mulder to multi-year deal |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/warriors-sign-canadian-mychal-mulder-multi-year-deal/ |access-date=March 10, 2020 |work=Sportsnet |date=March 10, 2020}} On April 28, 2021, Mulder had a career-high 26 points and five rebounds in a 133–103 loss against the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. On May 6, 2021, Mulder had 25 points in 20 minutes in a 118–97 win against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. On May 14, 2021, Mulder started for the Warriors and had a new career-high of 28 points in a 125–122 win against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. Mulder was waived near the end of training camp before the [[2021–22 NBA season|2021–22 season]].{{cite web|title=Warriors Waive Bell, Bradley, Mulder and Payton II|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/bell-bradley-mulder-payton-waived-20211015|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2021|access-date=October 16, 2021}} ===Orlando Magic (2021–2022)=== On October 26, 2021, the [[Orlando Magic]] signed Mulder to a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Mychal Mulder to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-mychal-mulder-free-agent-two-way-contract-20211026|website=NBA.com|date=October 26, 2021|access-date=October 26, 2021}} On January 6, 2022, he was waived.{{Cite web|title=Orlando Magic sign Admiral Schofield to a two-way contract, and waive Mychal Mulder|url=https://twitter.com/Magic_PR/status/1479204704991301640|access-date=January 6, 2022|website=Twitter.com}} ===Return to Sioux Falls (2022)=== On March 3, 2022, Mulder signed with the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web |title=SKYFORCE ACQUIRES MYCHAL MULDER |url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-mychal-mulder/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 4, 2022 |date=March 3, 2022}} ===Miami Heat (2022)=== On March 24, 2022, Mulder signed a two-way contract with the [[Miami Heat]].{{Cite web |title=Heat sign Mychal Mulder to 10-day contract, waive Kyle Guy |url=https://hoopshype.com/rumor/heat-sign-mychal-mulder-to-10-day-contract-waive-kyle-guy/ |access-date=March 24, 2022 |website=HoopsHype}} On July 16, he was waived.{{Cite web |title=HEAT SIGN DAYS AND GARRETT TO TWO-WAY CONTRACTS |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-days-and-garrett-to-two-way-contracts-071622 |access-date=July 16, 2022 |website=NBA}} On October 9, 2022, Mulder was re-signed by the Heat.{{cite web |title=HEAT CONVERT CAIN TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT AND SIGN MULDER |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-convert-cain-two-way-sign-mulder |website=NBA.com |date=October 9, 2022 |access-date=October 11, 2022}} ===Third stint with Skyforce (2022–2023)=== On October 24, 2022, Mulder rejoined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] roster for training camp.{{cite web|title=SKYFORCE ANNOUNCES TRAINING CAMP ROSTER AHEAD OF 2022-23 SEASON|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-training-camp-roster-ahead-of-2022-23-season/|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}} ===Memphis Hustle (2023)=== On September 1, 2023, Mulder's rights were traded to the [[Memphis Hustle]]{{cite web|title=Memphis Hustle Complete Trade with Sioux Falls Skyforce|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/memphis-hustle-complete-trade-with-sioux-falls-skyforce/n-6008996|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=September 1, Mulder|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-matthew-hurt-and-mychal-mulder|website=NBA.com|date=September 30, 2023|access-date=October 1, 2023}} However, he was waived on 2023|access-date=October 16, 2023}} and on October 30, he joined the Hustle.{{cite web|title=Memphis Hustle announce 2023-24 training camp roster|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 7, 2023}} ===Capital City Go-Go (2024)=== On December 27, 2023, Mulder was traded to the [[Capital City Go-Go]] in exchange for [[DeJon Jarreau]].{{cite web|title=Capital City Go-Go Complete Two Trades; Acquire Mychal Mulder and Taylor Funk|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/capital-city-go-go-complete-two-trades-acquire-mychal-mulder-and-taylor-funk|website=NBA.com|date=December 26, 2023|access-date=January 10, 2024}} ===Vancouver Bandits (2026–present)=== On March 26, 2026, Mulder signed with the [[Vancouver Bandits]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]] (CEBL) for the 2026 season.{{cite news
